tieu_de: Uranus transit through the 7th house: partnerships under new terms
mo: Will Uranus in the 7th house lead to divorce?
Is it a bad time to get married?
My partner has changed so much. What is going on?

A partner who announces they want to travel alone for a month. A business deal that appears out of nowhere. A friend you thought you knew who suddenly changes direction. When Uranus crosses into the 7th house, the people you commit to become less predictable, and so do you.

This transit is famous for testing marriages and close partnerships, and that reputation is partly deserved. What it tests, though, is not love. It tests whether each person has enough room to grow inside the arrangement.

doan: The 7th house covers one-to-one relationships: marriage, long-term partners, business partners and close friends who function almost like partners. It also describes the qualities you look for in others. Uranus here brings a strong need for freedom and novelty into those bonds.

Sometimes you are the one who wants change. Sometimes it is the other person. Often it is both at once. If a relationship has become confining or leaves no space for either of you to develop, the pressure to break or reshape it rises, especially around the time Uranus crosses the Descendant, the cusp of the 7th house.
Planet Uranus Rules Aquarius Innovation, freedom, surprise
Sudden changes in how a partner behaves, dresses or spends time.
Your own impatience with roles you once accepted in a relationship.
Unexpected new people entering your life with instant chemistry.
Business partnerships forming fast, or ending fast.
Conversations about space, freedom or an unconventional arrangement.
Attraction to people who are very different from your past partners.

Relationships can become more honest and more equal. Couples who come through this transit together often describe the bond afterwards as lighter and more genuine, because each person gained room to be themselves. Old unspoken deals, like one partner always making the decisions, can be renegotiated.

New connections formed now tend to be inspiring. They may bring you into contact with ideas, places and ways of life that expand your sense of what a relationship can be. In business, unusual partnerships can open doors that a more cautious alliance would not.

Stability does not come automatically. Relationships that begin suddenly under Uranus can be hard to sustain unless you build a real foundation underneath the excitement. Existing relationships that relied on things staying the same may feel strain, and some do end.
There is also a temptation to project Uranus onto the other person, blaming a partner for being unreliable while ignoring your own restlessness. Both sides usually contribute.

Uranus spends about 7 years in a sign, and a 7th house transit usually lasts several years, though the length depends on your house system and birth latitude. The period around the Descendant crossing and any Uranus aspects to your Venus or Sun tend to be the most intense.
Talk about freedom openly before it turns into resentment. Ask what each of you needs more room for.
Try changes inside the relationship first: separate hobbies, new shared projects, different living arrangements.
With new partners, enjoy the spark but give the foundation time before making permanent commitments.
In business, put agreements in writing, including how either party can exit.
Notice which of your complaints about others are really about your own need for change.
It raises the chance of separation when a relationship leaves no room for growth, but it does not guarantee it. Many couples use this period to redesign their partnership and come out stronger.
Not necessarily, but relationships formed under this transit move fast. If you marry, choose someone who respects your independence and whom you have seen in more than one kind of situation.

Uranus in your 7th often shows up through the people close to you. Your partner may be going through their own awakening. Curiosity and honest conversation work better than trying to pull them back to who they were.
